definitions.explanation: An establishment that cuts hair and shaves the face, licensed under barbering ({理容|りよう}) regulations. A formal, official-sounding term; in everyday speech people more often say {床屋|とこや} or {美容院|びよういん}.

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}の{理容店|りようてん}に{行|い}く。
examples.english: I'm going to the barbershop in front of the station.

examples.japanese: {理容店|りようてん}では{散髪|さんぱつ}と{顔|かお}そりをしてもらえる。
examples.english: At a barbershop you can get a haircut and a face shave.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{何十年|なんじゅうねん}も{同|おな}じ{理容店|りようてん}に{通|かよ}っている。
examples.english: My grandfather has gone to the same barbershop for decades.

notes:
A formal term for a barbershop, common on signs and in official contexts. Barbershops are licensed separately from beauty salons ({美容院|びよういん}) and may shave customers with a razor.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {理容店|りようてん}に{行|い}く: to go to the barbershop
- {理容店|りようてん}を{営|いとな}む: to run a barbershop

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {床屋|とこや}: barbershop — the casual everyday word for the same place
- {理髪店|りはつてん}: barbershop — another formal synonym
- {美容院|びよういん}: beauty salon — does styling and perms; legally distinct from a barbershop
